title: Senior Systems Engineer
description:
As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will be responsible for the technical outcome of complex space missions.  During mission contracting and requirements development, you may work with the sales engineering org to ensure mission requirements are valid and mission scope is adequately defined. Systems Engineers translate higher level requirements down to lower-level requirements, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary.    

You will be the overall technical lead responsible for "building the right thing" and "building it right". This will include the management of system requirements, technical budgets, and sub-system interfaces.  Your responsibility extends to ensuring there is sufficient verification and testing of the system, and you will take ownership of the technical performance outcomes for the mission. You will be the mission's technical lead for both Spire-internal and external (customer, contractor, etc) teams, working collaboratively with others to resolve technical discrepancies in requirements, specifications, or system performance.   

You will also act as the technical point of contact for Spire's global customers during mission development phases and through on-orbit validation of the space systems, working with Spire project and program managers to provide effective communication where required.   

Your knowledge and experience working across multiple technical disciplines will help you coordinate Spire's technical efforts to ensure ultimate mission success. 
  

Role Responsibilities:  

  • Take overall technical ownership of Spire Space and/or Ground Systems from technical development through on-orbit verification; ensure that we are "building the right thing" and "building it right". 
  • Lead requirements management for a given mission or program - including development, validation, verification, and change management. 
  • Lead technical risk management for a given mission or program - including identification, qualification, mitigation, and resolution. 
  • Develop top-level requirements and then flow-down to lower-levels, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary. 
  • Serve as the primary Spire technical POC to customers and contractors - communicating and advocating on behalf of internal technical teams where necessary. 
  • Serve as the customer's technical representative to Spire-internal teams - communicating and sometimes advocating for customer requirements, expectations, and experiences. 
  • Develop working knowledge of Spire's satellite platforms, operations systems, and payloads (both Spire and customer-developed) - including customer APIs and software service interfaces. 
  • Proactively communicate to program/project managers where changes in scope, requirements, expected system performance, or development outcomes impact the mission. 
  • Develop, deliver, and maintain mission documentation required to support programs or missions, including both internal and external (customer- or contractor-facing) documentation. 
  • Support the sales engineering team in the development of technical concepts and budgets, feasibility assessments, requirements, scope, and documentation needed during the sales cycle.  

Basic Qualifications:  

  • BSc in Engineering, Computer Science, equivalent STEM-related subject, or equivalent work experience. 
  • 5+ years of experience working in a technical engineering discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, RF Communications, etc) or as a systems engineer for complex integrated systems. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of space systems, concepts of operations, and remote systems operation.  

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 3+ years of experience as a space systems engineer working across engineering disciplines (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, Radio/Comms, etc) 
  • Experience developing or integrating RF and optical payloads. 
  • Experience participating in architecture and design of digital systems including ground station networks, data distribution and data processing systems, and spacecraft data handling systems 
  • Experience coordinating or leading diverse technical teams spanning multiple engineering disciplines and time zones 
  • Strong interpersonal skills for building relationships with clients and effectively communicating with other members of cross-functional teams 
  • Strong comprehension skills to enable timely understanding of complex customer requirements and identification of thorough and sometimes unique solutions 
  • Experience in satellite mission design, development, and testing with a clear understanding of major mission design trades and scope drivers (power / payload duty cycle, communications systems / data budgets, ground stations, launch and environmental loads, EMI/EMC, thermal management, etc.)  

 

Spire operates a hybrid work model, and this position will require you to work a minimum of three days per week in the office.

Access to US export-controlled software and/or technology may be required for this role. If needed, Spire will arrange the necessary licenses—this is not something candidates need to have before applying.  #LI-MK1

Spire Global is a space-to-cloud analytics company that owns and operates the largest multi-purpose constellation of satellites. title: Chief of Staff
description:
Your mission

We are looking for an experienced and entrepreneurial Chief of Staff (f/m/d) to join the leadership team at deeploi.

In this role, you act as a strategic and operational partner to the CEO, driving cross-functional alignment, owning our financial steering, and making sure decisions are taken and executed across the company.

You combine sharp financial judgment with organisational excellence, acting as a bridge between strategy, finance and execution, as we build deeploi into a company with sustainable, profitable growth.

This is a highly visible role with a wide scope. Wherever a topic matters and has no clear home, you take it, own it end to end, and drive it to a result. You set a high bar for yourself and the people around you.

Your Responsibilities

  • Own strategic projects: Lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives from first structure to final delivery.
  • Shape our commercial model: Drive how we position, package and price our product as we expand our SaaS offering and open up new go-to-market tiers.
  • Lead financial steering & reporting: Own business planning, forecasts, investor reporting and performance tracking, as well as accounting, billing and our external finance partners.
  • Structure how we run: Drive OKRs, decision-making and cross-functional collaboration for clarity and accountability, shape the formats that hold the team together and, together with People, connect company OKRs to performance management and feedback.
  • Partner with leadership: Act as a trusted thought partner to the Founders and the leadership team, including sparring on People initiatives.
  • Own legal & contracts: Take responsibility for customer contracts and contractual updates, coordinate external legal support, manage our public funding topics and drive our ISO topics.


Your profile

  • 5+ years of experience in consulting, investment or strategic and finance roles in a startup or scale-up, for example as a Chief of Staff, in a founder’s office, or in a senior finance role.
  • Strong background in financial analysis, reporting and planning, and confident in Excel modelling. Specialist accounting expertise is not required.
  • A real appetite to grab topics, take full accountability and drive them end to end, without waiting for someone to hand you a plan. You own what is unclear, unowned, and what everyone avoids.
  • Hands-on and entrepreneurial, with the detail orientation to push until something is excellent and the standards to raise the bar around you.
  • Excellent strategic thinking and communication: you translate between strategy, finance and operations, and challenge constructively at senior level.
  • Comfortable in a high performance culture with fast pace, changing priorities and broad responsibility.
  • High integrity, trustworthiness and discretion in handling sensitive information.
  • Fluent German (ideally C2) and business fluent English (C1).
  • You are in our Berlin office 3 to 4 days a week, and you make in-person culture something people want, not something they comply with.


Why us?

  • A key role in the leadership team with real ownership, impact and visibility, working directly alongside both Founders on the topics that decide where deeploi goes next.
  • Join a B2B SaaS company backed by Atomico, Cherry Ventures and other leading investors.
  • Competitive compensation package including virtual equity (VSOP).
  • Well-equipped offices in Berlin and Munich, plus benefits such as Urban Sports Club/EGYM or a public transport ticket and Corporate Benefits.
  • A team culture that is ambitious, transparent and collaborative, where ownership meets impact.

We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading venture capital investors including TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum, and Northzone, and are headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.

We are looking for our first dedicated Application Security Engineer to build our AppSec practice from the ground up. This is a greenfield opportunity with a real attack surface: public partner-facing APIs, payment flows, and active bug bounties. You will own secure development, define what gets reviewed, implement security gates, build the "paved road" for ~150 engineers, and see the impact of your work in production within weeks.

What you will do:

  • Lead threat modeling and secure design reviews for high-risk changes, partner integrations, and payment flows.

  • Implement, tune, and enforce security gates in GitLab CI/CD (SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, and DAST) while minimizing developer friction.

  • Act as the primary technical owner for triaging, reproducing, and prioritizing findings from bug bounties, partner pentests, and automated scanners.

  • Work hands-on with the DevOps team to implement GCP organizational policies, IAM least-privilege architectures, and Cloud Armor (WAF/rate limiting).

  • Establish a security-champions network across engineering squads and leverage automation/AI-assisted tooling to scale code reviews effectively.

Workplace:

We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe.

Also, the HQ office is in Berlin, where the team often meets.


Who you are:

  • You bring 5+ years in AppSec (or 3+ years plus a strong software engineering/web-pentesting background), with a track record of true ownership.

  • You read and write production code (Python, Go, TypeScript, Ruby, etc.) and deeply understand web frameworks, CI/CD, and Kubernetes.

  • You have deep knowledge of web and API security, specifically authentication/authorization models (OAuth2, JWT), rate limiting, tenant isolation, IDOR, and XSS.

  • You have strong cloud security fundamentals (GCP preferred), specifically regarding public exposure, secrets hygiene, and WAF rules.

  • You prioritize by real-world risk, propose trade-offs rather than demanding perfection, and communicate complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership.

  • Bonus Points: You have experience securing high-volume, multi-tenant B2B APIs and utilizing AI tooling to accelerate triage and review.

What you can expect:

  • You will join a fast-paced travel tech company with a flat organizational structure.

  • You will have exciting opportunities, ownership, and responsibility and contribute directly to the success of the company.

  • You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day!

  • We have a flexible work policy with the option of working remotely and international opportunities arising as we continue to expand our global footprint – Our heart is in Berlin, but you’ll find us across the globe.

  • You will get a competitive salary.

title: Head of Engineering (m/f/d)
description:
What we are building

ecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.


Why This Role Matters

You lead engineering at ecoplanet: 11 engineers in two squads, including two squad leads.

This is the most senior engineering role in the company. There is no CTO above you. You own the technical direction, not just the delivery of someone else's plan, and you are the engineering voice on the leadership team.

It is also a hands-on job. With a team this size you stay close to the code and the architecture. If you have been away from technical work for a few years, this might not be the right role for you.

What you will own:

  • The team. 11 engineers, which includes two engineering managers. Hiring, performance, growth, and keeping good people
  • The systems. Our Cockpit SaaS platform, the metering and IoT integration layer, the data platform (time-series ingestion, quality, pipelines), the forecasting and optimization services, and the automation that acts on customer assets
  • The technical direction. Architecture, build-vs-buy, and the big platform calls
  • Delivery. Quarterly roadmap execution, owned together with Product
  • Operations. Reliability, on-call, incidents, security posture, and cloud spend


What You’ll Achieve

  • Get the best out of the team you have and grow only where it clearly adds. At 11 people, losing one strong engineer costs more than one extra hire gains. But you should be capable of growing the team substantially if business demands it
  • Turn the roadmap into commitments the company can count on. Surface dependencies early, clear blockers, and make the trade-off calls with Product and the founders.
  • We expect engineering to care about business and product and we expect you to be an example here
  • Set the architecture so it holds as data volume, customer count and the team grow.
  • Run incidents properly: fast response, honest postmortems, fixes that stop the same thing happening again
  • Keep enough processes to be reliable and no more. A 11-person team should not feel like a 100-person one
  • Work closely with Product, Data Science, our energy market experts and other disciplines, so we build against the real physical and regulatory constraints


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have

  • 3+ years of experience leading engineering teams before in a product company, including senior engineers or squad leads
  • You have done it in a lean team, hands-on, without a layer of managers to delegate to. Some excellent large-company leaders struggle here. There is no layer to hide behind
  • You have personally owned delivery predictability and reliability for a production system real customers depend on, and you can tell us what it looked like before and after
  • Strong technical judgment in at least two of: cloud and distributed backend / multi-tenant SaaS; high-volume or time-series data pipelines; IoT, device integration and real-time telemetry; ML or optimization in production. Deep enough to earn engineers' trust, make architecture calls and set the technical direction yourself
  • You have run hiring and performance for real: you have grown people, and you have also managed people out when that was the right call
  • You treat incident management, security and compliance as yours to own, not to delegate
  • Clear written and spoken English. German is a strong plus — most of our customers are German Mittelstand
Nice to have
  • Energy, industrial, SaaS or a physical-world domain.
  • Having been the most senior technical person somewhere before (CTO, VP Engineering, or the person everyone asked).
Not required
  • Being the strongest coder on the team. You do need to read the code, make architecture calls, and occasionally build something.
  • A “Head of” title already. We look at what you have done, not what it was called.


What You Get

  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Competitive salary
  • Full ownership from day one — you actively shape our company
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership
  • Regular 1:1s and retros focused on your growth
  • Real impact — your work supports Europe's transition to a smarter energy system

description:
What we are building

At ecoplanet, we're redefining energy for tomorrow. Our mission: turn energy management into the competitive edge every European business relies on to win its market. We're building the operating system for the energy transition — cutting energy costs, improving efficiency, and streamlining operations. Backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and more, and built by a team full of top-tier talent.


Why This Role Matters

You will build and run the data backbone the whole product sits on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to get that data in clean, on time, and in a shape that dashboards, insights and forecasts can rely on.

You will join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.


What You’ll Achieve

  • Meter data integration. Connect industrial hardware and utility data streams into real-time dashboards. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is bringing data into a consistent structure across all sites
  • Anomalies and insights. This is where data science comes in. Find the things in the data a customer would want to know about — a meter drifting, a machine left running overnight, consumption that does not fit the pattern — and turn them into something they can act on
  • Tech stack and growth. Support the engineering team building scalable data pipeline


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • At least 3–5 years in a data engineering role or something close to it, building pipelines other people depend on

  • Hands-on data science experience. You do not need a research background. You do need to have built and evaluated models yourself: enough to tell a real anomaly from noise, to judge when a finding is solid enough to put in front of a paying customer, and to know what a pipeline owes a model running in production

  • Solid with Python and SQL and cloud data infrastructure. You have designed and run pipelines, APIs and workflows in production

  • Comfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readings

  • You think end to end before you go deep. title: Werkstudent KI & Automatisierung (m/w/d)
description:
Prozesse verstehen. Lösungen bauen, die bei KMUs tatsächlich laufen.

Warum es diese Stelle gibt

Wir sind ein kleines Team in Neumarkt und entwickeln IoT-Cloud-Lösungen für Maschinen- und Fahrzeughersteller. Parallel bauen wir eine Automatisierungsplattform, mit der wir Prozesse automatisieren – für uns selbst und für unsere Kunden. Mit KI-Agenten, LLM-Anbindungen und der Integration bestehender Fachsysteme.

Der Bedarf ist größer als das, was wir nebenbei erledigen können. Deshalb suchen wir jemanden, der genau daran arbeitet: bestehende Prozesse aufnehmen, verstehen wo es klemmt, und dann eine Lösung bauen, die läuft.

Was wir nicht suchen: jemanden, der Konzepte schreibt, die niemand umsetzt. Und keine Forschungsprojekte. Unsere Lösungen müssen zu einem Mittelständler passen – also einfach genug, dass sie auch ohne dich weiterlaufen.

Aufgaben

Was du machst

  • Prozesse aufnehmen. Du sprichst mit den Menschen, die einen Prozess täglich durchlaufen – bei uns oder beim Kunden. Du hältst fest, wie er heute wirklich läuft (nicht, wie er laut Handbuch laufen sollte), wo Zeit verloren geht und was am Ende besser sein soll.
  • Konzipieren. Du entscheidest, welcher Teil sich automatisieren lässt, wo KI echten Mehrwert bringt und wo eine einfache Regel genügt. Du schätzt Aufwand und Nutzen ab und legst dem Prozessowner eine Empfehlung vor – keine Optionsliste.
  • Umsetzen, hands-on. Du baust die Lösung selbst: KI-Agenten auf Basis von LLM-APIs, Automatisierungs-Workflows, Anbindung bestehender Systeme über REST-Schnittstellen und Webhooks, dazu die nötige Datenaufbereitung. Und ein Skript in Python oder JavaScript, wo Klicken nicht reicht.
  • Review und Übergabe. Du gehst mit dem Prozessowner durch, ob die Lösung im Alltag hält. Du prüfst nach, dokumentierst so, dass eine andere Person daran weiterarbeiten kann, und übergibst sauber.

Qualifikation

Was du mitbringen musst

  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch. Du führst Prozessgespräche mit Anwendern und Prozessownern, teils bei Kunden im Mittelstand. Das geht nicht auf Englisch. Verhandlungssicher heißt: du diskutierst frei, auch wenn es fachlich und sprachlich kompliziert wird.
  • Mindestens ein Tag pro Woche vor Ort in Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz. Prozessaufnahme funktioniert im Gespräch, nicht im Ticketsystem. Die übrige Zeit arbeitest du flexibel und remote.
  • Echte Begeisterung für KI und erste eigene Erfahrung damit. Kein Zertifikat, kein Studienschwerpunkt – aber du musst schon einmal selbst etwas mit KI gebaut haben. Ein Agent, ein LLM-Workflow, ein Chatbot auf eigenen Daten, ein Automatisierungsskript mit angebundenem Modell. Wir fragen im Gespräch danach, und zwar im Detail.

Dazu:

  • laufendes Studium – Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informatik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Technologie- oder Innovationsmanagement oder etwas Vergleichbares. Die Fachrichtung ist uns weniger wichtig als deine Arbeitsweise.
  • Du hast eine Sache schon einmal zu Ende gebaut – nicht nur angefangen.
  • Du kannst dich in einen fremden Prozess hineindenken und die richtigen Fragen stellen.
  • Du schreibst so, dass andere es verstehen.

Was wir gerne sehen, aber nicht erwarten

  • Praxis mit LangChain, LangGraph oder vergleichbaren Agenten-Frameworks
  • Erfahrung mit RAG, Vektordatenbanken oder Prompt Engineering über Spielerei hinaus
  • Grundlagen in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript und SQL
  • Arbeit mit KI-Coding-Tools wie Claude Code, GitHub Copilot oder Cursor

Ausdrücklich kein Muss: n8n. Wir arbeiten damit, aber diesen Teil deckt eine Kollegin bereits ab. Wenn du es kennst, gut – wenn nicht, lernst du es hier in wenigen Tagen.

Benefits

Was du bekommst

  • Echte Verantwortung für eigene Prozesse – vom ersten Gespräch bis zum Livegang. Keine Zuarbeit.
  • Anleitung durch unser Senior-Team, aber viel Freiraum in der Umsetzung.
  • Arbeit mit aktuellen KI- und Automatisierungswerkzeugen an produktiven Systemen, nicht an Sandkastenprojekten.
  • Kleines Team, kurze Wege, Entscheidungen am selben Tag.
  • 15–20 Stunden pro Woche im Semester, in den Semesterferien nach Absprache mehr.

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar Sätze zu einer KI- oder Automatisierungslösung, die du selbst gebaut hast: Wie lief der Prozess vorher, was hast du gebaut, welches Modell oder Tool hast du eingesetzt und warum, was war danach besser? Wenn es dazu ein Repository oder eine kurze Demo gibt, umso besser.

Wir betreiben in Norddeutschland (Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Brandenburg) mehrere Baustoffhandlungen und hagebaumärkte. Weitere Informationen über uns finden Sie unter www.schroeder-bauzentrum.de.

Zur Unterstützung unseres Teams suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt einen Werkstudenten (m/w/d) im Bereich Arbeitssicherheit und technisches Facility Management an unserem Standort Flensburg.



Ihre Aufgaben

  • Unterstützung der Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit im Tagesgeschäft

  • Erstellung, Pflege und Aktualisierung von Katastern, Übersichten und Dokumentationen

  • Unterstützung bei der Überwachung und Nachverfolgung gesetzlicher und technischer Prüfpflichten

  • Pflege von Prüfterminen sowie Nachverfolgung von Prüfberichten, festgestellten Mängeln und vereinbarten Maßnahmen

  • Aufbereitung und Verwaltung von Wartungs-, Prüf- und Anlagendokumentationen

  • Unterstützung bei der Erstellung von Gefährdungsbeurteilungen, Betriebsanweisungen und Unterweisungsunterlagen

  • Mitarbeit bei organisatorischen und technischen Projekten im Facility Management

  • Abstimmung mit unseren Standorten, internen Ansprechpartnern und externen Dienstleistern

Ihr Profil

  • Laufendes Studium, idealerweise in den Bereichen Sicherheitstechnik, Facility Management, Ingenieurwesen, Umweltmanagement oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung

  • Interesse an den Themen Arbeitssicherheit und technisches Facility Management

  • Technisches Verständnis und die Bereitschaft, sich in gesetzliche Vorgaben und technische Regelwerke einzuarbeiten

  • Führerschein der Klasse B sowie die Bereitschaft zu gelegentlichen Fahrten an unsere Standorte sind wünschenswert

Was wir Ihnen bieten

  • Eine abwechslungsreiche und praxisnahe Tätigkeit in einer starken Unternehmensgruppe

title: Social Media & Brand Growth Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Über ENUSEN

ENUSEN ist eine junge Nutrition-Marke aus Deutschland mit einer klaren Idee: moderne Ernährung soll zu echten Lebensmomenten passen – unkompliziert, hochwertig und relevant für Menschen mit einem aktiven Alltag.

Mit Smart Balance entwickeln wir aktuell unsere erste Produktlinie – eine neue Form moderner Daily Nutrition zwischen klassischem Snack und vollständiger Mahlzeit.

Für den Aufbau unserer Marke und den bevorstehenden Marktlaunch suchen wir eine Persönlichkeit, die Social Media nicht nur verwaltet, sondern eine junge Marke sichtbar macht, eine Community aufbaut und Menschen für sie begeistert.

Aufgaben

Deine Rolle

Als Social Media & Brand Growth Manager (m/w/d) gestaltest du den Social-Media-Auftritt von ENUSEN von Anfang an mit.

Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Head of Brand & Growth relevante Content-Formate, baust unsere Social-Media-Kanäle und Community auf und entwickelst ein Netzwerk aus Creatorn, Influencern und Markenbotschaftern.

Dabei suchen wir ausdrücklich keinen reinen Strategen. Wir möchten jemanden, der Ideen entwickelt und sie auch selbst umsetzt.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung unserer Social-Media-Kanäle, insbesondere Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn und YouTube
  • Entwicklung von Content- und Redaktionsplänen passend zur Brand- und Launchstrategie
  • Konzeption und Umsetzung von Social-Media-Content, Reels, Short Videos, Stories und weiteren digitalen Formaten
  • Aufbau und Betreuung eines Creator-, UGC- und Influencer-Netzwerks
  • Identifikation, Ansprache und Koordination geeigneter Creator und Kooperationspartner
  • Entwicklung von Creator Briefings und Begleitung von Kooperationen von der Idee bis zur Veröffentlichung
  • Aufbau und aktive Weiterentwicklung unserer Community
  • Planung und Begleitung von Foto-, Video-, Interview- und Content-Produktionen
  • Unterstützung bei PR, Brand Partnerships, Events, Sampling- und Launch-Aktivitäten
  • Zusammenarbeit mit externen Agenturen, Freelancern und Dienstleistern
  • Beobachtung relevanter Social-, Consumer- und Content-Trends
  • Analyse der Performance unserer Inhalte und kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung auf Basis relevanter KPIs
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Brand & Growth, E-Commerce und Geschäftsführung

Qualifikation

Dein Profil

  • 2-5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung im Bereich Social Media, Influencer/Creator Marketing, Content, Community oder Brand Communication
  • Erfahrung mit Influencer Marketing, Creator Relations und UGC
  • Sehr gutes Verständnis für Instagram, TikTok und aktuelle Content-Formate
  • Du kannst nicht nur Konzepte schreiben, sondern Inhalte und Kampagnen auch praktisch umsetzen
  • Sicheres Gespür für Sprache, Storytelling, Bildwelten und Markenkommunikation
  • Erfahrung mit Tools wie Canva, CapCut, Premiere Pro oder vergleichbaren Anwendungen ist von Vorteil
  • Idealerweise Erfahrung in Nutrition, Consumer Health, Food, FMCG, Beauty, Lifestyle oder D2C
  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem bzw. C2-Niveau und sehr gutes Englisch
  • Eigeninitiative, Kreativität und Freude daran, Strukturen nicht nur zu übernehmen, sondern selbst mit aufzubauen

Benefits

Was wir bieten

  • Die Möglichkeit, eine neue Consumer Brand von Beginn an aktiv mitzugestalten
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unserem Head of Brand & Growth und der Geschäftsführung
  • Kurze Entscheidungswege und viel eigener Gestaltungsspielraum
  • Verantwortung statt starrer Konzernstrukturen
  • Ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem gute Ideen schnell umgesetzt werden können
  • Zusätzlich Teilnahme an unserem Performance-Bonus-Pool, orientiert an individueller Leistung sowie dem Beitrag zum Unternehmens- und Absatzwachstum
  • Langfristige Entwicklungs- und Wachstumsmöglichkeiten gemeinsam mit ENUSEN

Was uns besonders wichtig ist

ENUSEN befindet sich noch am Anfang. Deshalb suchen wir keinen Menschen, der lediglich einen bestehenden Social-Media-Kalender weiterführt.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Freude daran hat, zu sagen:

„Ich war dabei, als diese Marke aufgebaut wurde.“

Du solltest Lust darauf haben, Dinge auszuprobieren, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, nah am Produkt und am Konsumenten zu arbeiten und gemeinsam mit einem kleinen Team aus einer Idee eine relevante Consumer Brand zu entwickeln.

Interesse?

Dann freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Bitte sende uns deinen Lebenslauf sowie – sofern vorhanden – gerne Beispiele von Social-Media-Kanälen, Content-Projekten, Creator-Kampagnen oder Marken, an denen du bereits gearbeitet hast.

title: Videograf / Content Producer (m/w/d)
description:
SKINBRO ist eine der am schnellsten wachsenden Männerpflege-Marken Deutschlands. Feste Duschseifen, Deos und Parfums – plastikfrei, made in Germany, mit Düften, die Männer wirklich wollen. Über 90.000 Kunden, in den letzten Monaten jeden Monat fast verdoppelt. Wir sitzen in Hamburg, sind ein kleines, schnelles Team und wachsen ohne Konzernstrukturen.

Unser Wachstum kommt aus Creatives. Aktuell produzieren wir rund 300 Ads im Monat mit einem Shooting pro Woche. Mit dir wollen wir auf drei Shootings pro Woche und über 1.000 Assets im Monat.

Spoiler: Wir suchen keinen klassischen Videografen und keinen Creative Director. Wir suchen die Person, die Ideen in die Realität bringt. Die Creative Strategie – Konzepte, Skripte, Angles, Briefings – kommt fertig vom Gründer. Du bekommst am Anfang der Woche deine Shooting-Pläne und ziehst sie von A bis Z durch. Um dich herum: externe Video-Editoren, ein Grafikdesigner, ein eingespielter Prozess.

Das ist eine ausführende Rolle, keine konzeptionelle. Wenn du lieber selbst die Strategie machen willst, ist das nicht die richtige Stelle. Wenn du Bock hast, in einer Creative-Maschine zu arbeiten, die bereits funktioniert, und sie mit uns zu verdreifachen – dann schon.

Aufgaben

Du führst 2–3 Shootings pro Woche eigenständig durch – ohne dass der Gründer am Set stehen muss.

Du organisierst alles drumherum: Location, Darsteller, UGC-Creator, Zeitplan, Equipment, Verpflegung.

Du sourcst regelmäßig neue Gesichter für Straßeninterviews, Schauspieler-Spots und UGC.

Du bedienst die Kamera selbst und lieferst sauberes, verwertbares Rohmaterial nach Briefing.

Du legst das Material strukturiert ab und übergibst es mit klarem Briefing an unsere Editoren.

Du gibst den Editoren fundiertes Feedback und schneidest bei Bedarf selbst.

Du analysierst gemeinsam mit dem Gründer, welche Creatives performt haben und welche nicht – und nimmst die Learnings mit ins nächste Shooting.

Qualifikation

Du kannst Shootings komplett selbstständig durchführen – Planung, Dreh, Ablage.

Du kannst editieren (Premiere, CapCut, DaVinci o. ä.) – gut genug, um Editoren präzise zu briefen, ihr Ergebnis zu bewerten und selbst Videos zu schneiden.

Du hast Feingefühl am Set: Du empfängst Leute, machst sie locker, korrigierst taktvoll und sorgst dafür, dass alle gerne wiederkommen – auch bei Skripten, die etwas frecher sind.

Du hast ein Gespür dafür, welche Person welche Aussage am glaubwürdigsten rüberbringt.

Du arbeitest strukturiert nach Prozess und Checkliste und hast kein Problem damit, Content in hoher Frequenz zu produzieren, ohne dass die Qualität leidet.

Du verstehst, was eine Performance-Ad von einem schönen Video unterscheidet – oder willst es schnell lernen.

Du wohnst in Hamburg oder bist bereit, hierher zu ziehen.

Benefits

Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit dem Gründer-Team.
Ads, die jeden Monat Millionen von Männern sehen – du siehst sofort, was dein Output bewirkt.

Keine Konzernstrukturen, kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen.

Büro direkt in der Hamburger-Innenstadt.

  • Erstellung und Analyse von Businessplänen, Cashflow-Modellen und Finanzierungsszenarien

  • Laufende Überwachung bestehender Finanzierungen, Covenants und Berichtspflichten
  • Mitwirkung bei Prolongationen, Refinanzierungen und Finanzierungsanpassungen

Erstellung regelmäßiger Finanzierungs- und Liquiditätsübersichten

Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem Leiter Finanzierung

Qualifikation

title: Account Executive
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Account Executive based in Germany.

This is a highly technical sales role focused on helping engineering teams adopt infrastructure and developer-focused technology.
You will own opportunities from initial engagement through close, working directly with technically sophisticated customers who expect credibility and speed.
The role combines consultative selling, technical problem-solving, proof-of-concept management, and disciplined pipeline ownership.
You will work closely with Solutions Engineers while becoming a trusted presence in customer communication channels and helping remove obstacles to purchase.
Success requires the confidence to explain complex concepts simply, challenge assumptions, and be transparent when a solution is not the right fit.
You will operate with significant autonomy in a fast-moving environment where experimentation, urgency, and customer outcomes matter.
This is an opportunity for either an experienced technical AE or a technically minded professional ready to take ownership of a sales quota.


Accountabilities
  • Own the sales process from qualified opportunity through successful close, with a strong focus on helping technical customers achieve their desired outcomes.
  • Build trusted relationships with engineers and technical stakeholders, including actively participating in customer communication channels such as Slack.
  • Manage and close inbound sales opportunities, moving prospects efficiently through the buying process.
  • Lead and coordinate proof-of-concept initiatives in partnership with Solutions Engineers, ensuring technical and commercial objectives are clearly defined.
  • Help customers troubleshoot questions and remove technical or commercial obstacles that could prevent a successful purchase.
  • Communicate honestly and transparently, including clearly explaining when a solution is not an appropriate fit.
  • Maintain a systematic approach to pipeline management, ensuring opportunities, next steps, and follow-ups are consistently tracked.
  • Navigate, improve, and contribute to internal sales and go-to-market systems and processes.
  • Experiment with new approaches to prospect engagement, deal execution, and GTM workflows, using results and customer feedback to continuously improve.
  • Move quickly and independently, identifying what needs to be done and taking action without requiring detailed direction.

    • Requirements

    • Proven experience as an Account Executive, particularly in a technical B2B, SaaS, infrastructure, or developer-focused sales environment; alternatively, strong technical experience combined with readiness to take on a sales quota.
    • Strong technical aptitude, including the ability to comfortably understand API documentation, technical product concepts, and engineering workflows.
    • Experience selling to developers or engineering teams is highly desirable, with an understanding of how to build credibility with technically sophisticated buyers.
    • Strong organizational and pipeline-management skills, with a systematic approach to tracking opportunities and following through on commitments.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and concisely.
    • High integrity and customer orientation, with a commitment to honest communication rather than overselling.
    • Strong sense of urgency and ability to operate at the pace of technically sophisticated, fast-moving customers.
    • Self-directed and resourceful, with the ability to take ownership and make progress without extensive supervision.
    • Curious and experimental mindset, with a willingness to test new approaches, learn from unsuccessful experiments, and adapt quickly.
    • Experience with databases, search technologies, or infrastructure software is a plus.
    • Familiarity with GTM automation tools such as Clay or n8n is advantageous.
    • Comfort working with Python, JavaScript, Linux, or major cloud platforms is a plus.
    • Willingness to prioritize correctness, customer evidence, initiative, and continuous improvement in day-to-day decision-making.

Als Medical Director verantwortest du den medizinischen Themenkatalog einer der größten CME-Lernplattformen Deutschlands. Was wir zeigen, erreicht unzählige Ärzt:innen – deine inhaltlichen Entscheidungen haben unmittelbaren Einfluss darauf, welches medizinische Wissen in Deutschland ankommt.

Your tasks

  • Verantwortung für den Themenkatalog: Du steuerst, welche medizinischen Themen wir abdecken – fachübergreifend, evidenzbasiert und mit einem klaren Blick für Versorgungsrelevanz und Lücken im Markt.

  • Qualitätssicherung & Compliance: Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Fortbildungen den CME-Standards entsprechen, evidenzbasiert sind und die regulatorischen Anforderungen erfüllen.

  • Prozessverbesserung & Automatisierung: Auf unserem Weg zum Scale-up stehen Automatisierung und schlanke Prozesse im Mittelpunkt. Du streamlinest Workflows und Dokumentationstools im Team und teamübergreifend – als Director bist du dabei die Schlüsselrolle für funktionierende Cross-Department-Zusammenarbeit.


Your profile

  • Hintergrund: Abgeschlossenes Studium der Medizin.

  • Berufserfahrung: Idealerweise 5+ Jahre Berufserfahrung, gern klinisch, in der Industrie oder in der digitalen Gesundheitsbranche.

  • Anpack-Mindset: Wir skalieren. Du regelst Dinge selbst, statt sie nur zu delegieren, und scheust dich nicht davor, auch operativ mit reinzugehen.

  • Begeisterung für Prozesse: Du hast Freude an Projektmanagement, Strukturaufbau und medizinischem Content bzw. medizinischer Lehre – diese Kombination ist der Kern der Rolle.

  • Von Vorteil: Erfahrung in einem Startup sowie in der medizinischen Lehre.

  • Kommunikationsstärke: Sicheres Auftreten gegenüber führenden Mediziner:innen und Industriepartnern, professioneller Kommunikationsstil mündlich und schriftlich.

  • Sprachen: Deutsch auf Muttersprachenniveau und fließendes Englisch sind Voraussetzung.


Why us?

  • Echter Impact: Die Themen, die du verantwortest, erreichen über zig tausende Ärzt:innen. Durch die Verbreitung des neuesten medizinischen Wissens hast du direkten Einfluss auf die Versorgungsqualität in Deutschland.

  • Mitgestaltung: Du prägst neue Fortbildungsformate und den medizinischen Qualitätsanspruch der Plattform von Grund auf mit.

  • Wachstum & Perspektive: Wir wachsen schnell – entsprechend gibt es echte Aufstiegs- und Gestaltungschancen, die mit dem Unternehmen mitwachsen.

  • Ownership: Kurze Entscheidungswege, flache Hierarchien und die Freiheit, eigene Ideen umzusetzen.

At Apheris, we are building the future of how AI is applied in pharmaceutical R&D. We enable leading pharmaceutical teams to discover and develop drugs faster. We host the industry’s largest federated data networks for drug discovery AI, spanning co-folding, ADMET, and antibody developability.

title: Senior HR Specialist - Recruiting & Onboarding (m/f/d) in Berlin or Konstanz
description:
Mission

Drive KNIME’s global growth by attracting, hiring, and onboarding top talent through data-informed and tech-driven recruitment strategies.


Role Overview

As an HR Specialist - Recruiting & Onboarding at KNIME, you will own the end-to-end recruitment cycle and deliver an exceptional onboarding experience for new team members. Partnering closely with hiring managers, you will optimize candidate pipelines using modern HR tech, ATS platforms, and AI-driven tools. This role offers the opportunity to shape recruitment marketing, foster diversity, and continually refine our hiring workflows in a fast-paced software environment.


Responsibilities

  • Partner with hiring managers to assess talent needs and drive the full end-to-end recruitment cycle.

  • Screen resumes, conduct initial phone screens, and lead behavioral interviews to evaluate technical baseline and cultural alignment.

  • Coordinate and schedule interviews while building strong relationships with candidates, hiring managers, and external partners.

  • Drive a diverse and inclusive recruitment strategy, supporting recruitment marketing and job ad promotion across relevant channels.

  • Maintain clean ATS records, analyze candidate funnels, and prepare hiring reports to guide recruitment decisions.

  • Manage operational pre-boarding and onboarding processes to deliver a smooth integration for new joiners.

  • Test, evaluate, and roll out AI tools to streamline sourcing, screening, and HR processes.


Requirements

  • Proven track record sourcing and hiring across both the US and German tech/software markets, with a solid understanding of the cultural and operational nuances of both regions. 

  • Hands-on experience with ATS tools (e.g., Personio or Ashby) and a high level of digital savviness.

  • Clear communication and active listening skills with a strong customer-centric focus on candidate and hiring manager experience.

  • Strong team player with an agile, pragmatic mindset and excellent organizational skills.

  • Practical interest in or active experience leveraging AI tools to optimize sourcing, candidate engagement, and onboarding. 

  • High standards of confidentiality and data integrity.

  • Fluency in both German and English.


What Success Looks Like

title: Senior Product Data Analyst - Consumer Growth
description:
About the team

SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.

As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.

We're looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You'll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.

You'll help answer questions such as:

  • Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?
  • Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?
  • What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?
  • Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?
  • How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?

If you're motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.
  • Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.
  • Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value.
  • Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities.
  • Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted.
  • Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement.

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar.
  • You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis.
  • You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value.
  • You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation.
  • You've worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them.
  • You're proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use.
  • You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • You're comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence.
  • You're curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making.
  • You're comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style.

This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

title: Commercial Lead - Clinical Trials
description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself then, choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

The role

We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business.

What you’ll do

  • Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital.

  • Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities.

  • Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction.

  • Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value.

  • Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery.

  • Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment.

  • Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable.

  • Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling.

  • Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise.

What you’ll need

The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience.

  • Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation.

  • A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites.

  • A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed.

  • Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment.

  • The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity.

  • The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team.

Additional strengths

  • Experience as a founder, early executive or leader who created a new clinical trials business or commercial proposition.

  • A strong network across pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, CROs, research sites, health systems, investigators or patient organisations.

  • Experience across more than one side of the ecosystem, such as sponsor and site, CRO and technology, or clinical practice and commercial delivery.

  • Experience selling enterprise software, technology enabled services, recruitment programmes or data products to life sciences organisations.

  • Product fluency and the ability to turn market evidence into useful guidance for product and engineering teams.

  • Familiarity with clinical research systems such as CTMS, EDC, eConsent, ePRO, trial registries and EHR or EMR integrations.

  • A clinical or scientific qualification. This can strengthen your credibility, but it is not a substitute for commercial results.

  • Experience with Australian, UK or comparable clinical research markets.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

title: Strategist, Agent Development (Norwegian speaking)
description:
About us

At Sierra, we’re building a platform to enable every company in the world to build better, more human customer experiences with AI. We partner with industry leaders such as SoftBank, Uber, Rivian, CLEAR, and Sutter Health. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and Family. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. 

What you'll do

As an Agent Strategist, you own how Sierra's AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. You transform a customer's thorniest, highest-stakes problems into agents that measurably move their business.

  • Own the Agent Development Life Cycle. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it's the best version of itself in the real world. You'll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

  • Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers' executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

  • Partner with the customer's working teams day to day. Run working sessions, troubleshoot the agent as issues come up, and make the calls that keep the build on track for launch.

  • Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.

Example projects

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

  • Scope and launch a subscription-retention agent for a large telecommunications or media company that consistently outperforms human agents at saving at-risk customers.

  • Stand up an agent for a commerce customer that troubleshoots a broken device end-to-end and personalizes product recommendations in the same conversation.

  • Redesign the conversation flows for a financial services agent so it can handle complex, regulated interactions — and convert a pilot into a multi-team production deployment. See our financial services blog for examples.

  • Partner with product on a net-new capability — a new agent architecture or self-service tooling — using a live customer as the design partner.

  • Define the evaluation and quality bar for a new agent, then use those metrics to drive a measurable lift in outcome week over week.

What you'll bring

  • Customer obsession. Genuine energy being in front of customers — understanding their business and needs, thriving in complex organizations, and building trusted relationships.

  • Communication. Clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strategic problem-solving in ambiguity. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to break down complex problems, spot risks early, and adapt as things change fast.

  • Technical aptitude. Comfortable engaging directly with technical concepts - reading API documentation, understanding data models and system architecture, and following engineering tradeoffs in a design discussion.

  • Ownership and delivery. A track record of running multiple complex, high-visibility projects at once and driving them to outcomes.

Even better...

  • Experience building or deploying AI/LLM agents in production — hands-on with the tools behind them (eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering) — working closely with technical counterparts.

  • You've been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience — and/or an MBA or comparable experience at the intersection of technology and business.

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

  • Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

  • Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

  • Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

  • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

  • Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

  • Life insurance and disability benefits

  • Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

  • Parental leave

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

  • Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

  • Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Compensation: £150K – £245K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Backend Engineer

description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our award-winning Data Science team at a pivotal moment. Carwow operates a two-sided marketplace — connecting car buyers and sellers at scale — and data science sits at the heart of how we make that marketplace smarter, faster, and more valuable for everyone in it. In fact, we recently won GenAI initiative of the Year at the British Data Awards.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role working centrally across the business. You'll partner with teams spanning Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations — developing and deploying ML and AI solutions that drive outcomes across both sides of our marketplace. The problems you'll work on are genuinely varied: pricing models, propensity and demand signals that sharpen marketing spend, personalised recommendations for our web product and CRM, and LLM-powered solutions for operational challenges like document verification.

You'll translate ambiguous business problems into structured, production-ready solutions — and you'll be expected to deliver them end-to-end, from first principles through to being deployment-ready and beyond.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • End-to-End ML & AI Delivery: Lead data science initiatives from problem framing through to deployment, monitoring, and iteration — delivering the full production lifecycle. With no dedicated ML engineering function, you'll be responsible for ensuring your solutions are robust, scalable, and performing in the real world long after they ship.

  • GenAI & LLM Application: Design and build LLM-powered solutions where they create genuine business value — document processing, intelligent search, content understanding, and beyond. Apply them alongside classical ML with clear judgement about where each approach earns its place.

  • Commercial Impact: Connect your work directly to business outcomes. Whether you're building a model to improve marketing efficiency, a pricing signal to sharpen commercial decisions, or a recommendation engine to increase conversion — you understand the business lever you're pulling and design your solutions accordingly.

  • Prototyping & Experimentation: Move fast to test ideas before committing to full-scale development. Define rigorous success metrics upfront, validate honestly, and know when to double down and when to walk away.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations stakeholders to understand problems deeply before reaching for a solution. Translate findings into clear, actionable narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Standards & Craft: Contribute to shared best practices, documentation, and ways of working that raise the bar for the data science function — and help more junior team members grow alongside you. Drive continued adoption of AI capabilities to drive efficiencies, automation and constantly leverage new capabilities.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

Please note: We know that no candidate will be the perfect match for all we've listed in this posting, so we’d encourage you to apply if you feel you're close to the brief but not an exact match. Ideally you’ll have

  • Commercial Mindset: You think about business impact first. You understand how your models connect to revenue, efficiency, or customer outcomes — and you use that to prioritise, scope, and communicate your work.

  • Stakeholder Partnership: Proven ability to work with commercial, marketing, and product stakeholders — translating business problems into well-scoped solutions and communicating technical solutions, challenges and outcomes clearly at all levels.

  • Sound Judgement: You navigate the tooling landscape with clear eyes — knowing when classical ML is right, when GenAI unlocks something new, and when a simpler solution is the more honest answer. Strong instincts for scalability, reliability, and explainability.

  • [Bonus] Marketplace or Two-Sided Platform Experience: Understanding of supply/demand dynamics and how data science creates leverage in a marketplace context.

TEHCNICAL SKILLSET

  • Proven ML Experience: A strong track record of building, deploying, and maintaining ML models in Python in a production environment — not just notebooks. You've owned models after they ship and know how to keep them healthy.

  • Full-Lifecycle Delivery (MLOps): Comfortable delivering the end-to-end production lifecycle — model training, versioning, monitoring, and champion/challenger experimentation — without relying on a dedicated ML engineering team to carry that responsibility.

  • GenAI & LLM Expertise: Hands-on experience building LLM-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value. You understand how to apply, evaluate, and extend these tools — and you're honest about where they fall short.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Bookkeeper — Lab54

Location: London. All 3 days in office for the first three months. From month 4, 1 day per week remote once the agreed targets are being met.

Shape: Part-time, 3 days per week. Permanent or contract — both considered.

Salary: £30–34k FTE equivalent, pro-rata (£18–20.5k at 3 days). Contract equivalent £150–200 per day.

Reports to: Financial Controller (interim: Managing Director)

Start: As soon as available

About Lab54

Lab54 is a content-led events and production company: [Anywhere But A Club.]

We create high-impact experiences in unexpected locations, capture them, and turn them into content. Combined global audience of 425,000+. We work with brands, record labels and artists — around 100 events a year across brand activations, artist pop-ups, hard-ticket shows, house parties and festival takeovers.

The role

The Bookkeeper is Lab54's day-to-day finance function: reconciliation, purchase-order matching, receipt capture, invoicing, debtor chasing and payroll preparation.

The defining feature of the job is that every pound has to land against an event. Lab54's core financial object isn't the month — it's the project. Each event carries a code (YYMM-Owner-Event-City) that runs from HubSpot through Xero, Teamwork and the purchase-order flow. Coding transactions to that project is not admin; it's the thing that makes per-event profitability computable. It is the single most important part of this role.

This role prepares, never approves. All payment runs are approved by the Managing Director, with the CEO approving above an agreed threshold.

Responsibilities

Purchase orders and supplier ledger

  • Match supplier invoices to their purchase order in Xero. This is a manual link, and it is the control that stops us paying more than we agreed.
  • Enforce the PO rule at the front door: any commitment of £500 or more needs a PO, and an invoice arriving without a PO number goes back to the supplier rather than into the ledger.
  • Prepare payment runs for approval. Nothing leaves the business without a bill, a PO and a sign-off.
  • Reconcile supplier statements monthly against our purchase ledger — the check that catches duplicate invoices and payments before they're made.
  • Maintain the purchase ledger and keep the aged creditor position accurate.

Reconciliation and coding

  • Bank and card reconciliations kept current within 48 hours, including Revolut Business card spend against Xero tracking categories.
  • Every reconciled line matched to a real source document. A line that reconciles without a bill behind it is an exception to raise, not a box to tick.
  • Code every transaction to the correct project code and tracking category. Chase the team when a code is missing rather than guessing one.
  • Keep the suspense and uncoded accounts at nil by month-end.
  • Produce a weekly untagged-spend report, by spender, and drive it to zero.

Receipts and VAT recovery

  • Chase and capture missing receipts to a 98% target. This is a cash exercise, not a filing one — every missing VAT invoice is input VAT we can't reclaim.
  • Flag transactions carrying no VAT treatment where the supplier is UK VAT-registered.
  • Prepare the VAT return workings for the external accountancy firm, who own submission.

Sales invoicing and debtors

  • Raise client invoices within 48 hours of the billing trigger, coded to the project.
  • Own debtor chasing end to end — a consistent cycle, escalated when it stalls, so nobody else in the business is carrying it.
  • Match incoming receipts to the right invoice and contact. Money that arrives against the wrong customer looks identical to money that never arrived.
  • Keep sales invoice sequencing clean — anything voided or reissued carries a recorded reason.

Project close

  • When a project closes, produce its final position: budgeted cost against actual cost, budgeted revenue against invoiced revenue, and the resulting margin.
  • Issue that to the CEO and Operations Director as a matter of routine. It is not a report anyone should have to request.
  • Late costs land after an event has finished — that's the nature of the business. The job is to make sure they land against the right project and that the closing number reflects them.

Cash and reporting

  • Produce a weekly cash one-pager: bank position, overdue debtors with days outstanding, payment runs due, projected balance.
  • Keep the company's master P&L model current — updating actuals and committed costs as they change, so the forecast reflects where the business genuinely is.
  • The model is ours; you update the numbers within it. Structural or formula changes come to the CEO first.

Payroll preparation

  • Prepare payroll data and submit it to the external payroll provider ahead of deadline.
  • Post the payroll journal to Xero each month. Wages must not sit in a control account.
  • Confirm the payroll account is funded before each run. This role does not execute payroll.

Close, deadlines and records

  • Run the monthly close to a published working-day deadline: accruals prepared with supporting detail, journals posted, period locked.
  • Every accrual carries a schedule — supplier, event, date of work. No balance we can't explain.
  • Maintain the statutory deadline register (VAT, PAYE, corporation tax, Companies House) and flag each one in advance. No filing sits invisibly in someone else's workflow.
  • Keep records orderly and audit-ready for the external accountancy firm.

What the first 90 days actually look like

We are being straight about this because we want someone who finds it interesting rather than alarming.

Lab54 has grown faster than its finance function, and we've recently changed accountants. The ledger carries a real backlog: untagged transactions across two financial years, unposted payroll journals, a month-end close that has not been run to a cadence, and a purchase-order process that has only just gone live. There is a documented correction schedule and an external FD working through it.

The first 90 days is a clean-up, not a steady state.

Days 1–30. Learn the ledger and the project-code structure. Take over reconciliation, receipt capture and PO matching. Get the weekly untagged report running.

Days 31–60. Clear the untagged backlog. Take over sales invoicing, debtor chasing and received-payment matching. Payroll preparation and the monthly payroll journal move across.

Days 61–90. Run a full month close to deadline: suspense at nil, every accrual scheduled, supplier statements reconciled. Per-project cost data becomes reportable for the first time.

After that it becomes a genuinely well-defined job inside a documented control structure — and you'll have built it.

On being in the office. The first three months are fully office-based, and that's deliberate rather than a policy position. Clearing a backlog this size means asking people questions in real time — whose card that was, what the missing PO covers, which event a supplier belongs to. That's an hour of work in a room and a week of work over email. From month 4, one of the three days moves to remote, provided the measures below are being met.

You will translate our value vision into a scalable operating model by building automations, defining processes and ways of working, standing up KPIs and reporting, operationalising our internal ROI framework, feeding the feedback loop to capitalize on our successes, and embedding reusable value frameworks into customer engagements.

This role is critical to turning our go-to-market strategy into repeatable, AI-native action, aligning delivery quality, output per FTE, and customer satisfaction to improve the efficiency and impact of our Solutions organisation and accelerate the value Mistral delivers to customers.

 

What You Will Do

 

Operating System & Automation

  • Build the secure-by-design operating system that links our tooling stack to the Solutions team’s needs, and design the internal tools & automations that raise output per FTE.

  • Streamline Deployment Strategist operations across pre-sales scoping and delivery, compounding shared knowledge, templates, and reusable IP.

  • Drive daily adoption of our AI layer throughout the Solutions team, productising internal work into reusable assets for the team.

Value Intelligence & ROI

  • Operationalise the internal ROI framework per project / use case, defining and surfacing where we build value.

  • Define the reporting layer and metric catalog (what we collect and surface) and build the dashboards that turn our data foundation into decisions and proof of value.

  • Stand up the customer satisfaction measurement system (define, collect, surface) as a core input to value realization.

Processes, Ways of Working & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Codify delivery playbooks, ways of working, and scaling programs end-to-end across the customer lifecycle

  • Partner with Revenue Growth, People Growth, RevOps, CSMs and Product & Engineering to align the operating system with company strategy and fuel the flywheel.

  • Ensure our operational processes are followed across geographies, embedding safety, security & compliance into our ways of working.

 

What We're Looking For

  • 4+ years of experience in strategic operations, business operations, or a chief-of-staff role within technical sales or solutions engineering.

  • Strong ability to bring structure to ambiguity and drive complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution.

  • Proven track record in optimising processes, impacting business KPIs, and aligning resources with business priorities.

  • Exceptional negotiation and diplomacy skills: ability to navigate complex stakeholder dynamics and align competing priorities.

  • Hands-on, execution-focused mindset with a bias for action in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.

  • Hands-on builder of internal tools and data workflows; comfortable turning manual processes into scalable systems.
